__broaden__.αἱ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. pl. ’they’, referring to the ships (αἱ δ’ ... ἔπλεον) · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of women (αἱ δ’ ὅτε ... ἵκοντο ’and when they came’) · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of the mules (αἱ δ’ ὦκα λίπον ’and they quickly left’) · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of the islands (αἱ δέ τ’ ἄνευθε ’and they lie apart’) · also fem. nom. pl. with a noun, article-like: ’the others’ (αἱ ἄλλαι ’the other ships’) · also fem. nom. pl., correlative, of the doors: αἱ μὲν … αἱ δ’ ’the one … the other’ · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of the swine (αἱ δὲ νέμονται ’and they graze’) · also fem. nom. pl. with a noun, article-like: ’the’ (αἱ κύνες ’the dogs’) · also fem. nom. pl., correlative, of the maids: αἱ μὲν … αἱ δ’ ’some … others’, in orders ’some of you … others of you’ · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of the cattle (αἱ μὲν γίγνονται ’they grow’) · also fem. nom. pl., correlative, of the Achaean women: αἱ μὲν … αἱ δ’ ’some … others’ · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of the souls of the dead
